title: Lab results that break the contract
prompt: The lab-results feed has a contract with three rules. Write `solve(observations)` so it returns every observation that breaks at least one of them.
rules: `value` must be present and a real number: missing or NaN breaks the rule.
`unit` must be the unit of its `code`: GLU mg/dL, HBA1C %, LDL mg/dL, HGB g/dL, BMI kg/m2. Any other code, or a missing unit, breaks the rule.
An HBA1C `value` must be between 3 and 20, both included. Return every column of `observations`, unchanged.
hints: Write each rule as a condition that is true for a good row, then keep the rows where any rule is not true.
`F.isnan` catches NaN, which `isNull` doesn't. For the unit, a `F.when` chain can give the expected unit for each code.
Wrap each rule in `F.coalesce(rule, F.lit(False))` so a NULL counts as a failure instead of hiding the row.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(observations):
    # Return the observations that break at least one rule.
    return observations
